title: Degree under a coordinate sum factor
statement: Let $q$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube with Fourier degree at most $d$, and let $r\\in\\mathbb R$. The function $x\\mapsto q(x)\\bigl(\\sum_{i=1}^n x_i-r\\bigr)$ has Fourier degree at most $d+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function q on the Boolean cube
A natural number d such that the Fourier degree of q is at most d
